source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which community measure reduces the snail population to control schistosomiasis?
questions.rationale: Snail density is reduced with molluscicides and stream cleaning, which exposes snails to sunlight. Footbridges over infested streams also help.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Schistosomiasis Prevention (PDF p. 172)
questions.quote: Stream Cleaning Vegetation (expose the snails to sunlight)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which lesion is typical of PRIMARY syphilis?
questions.rationale: Primary syphilis presents a painless chancre at the site of entry with swollen glands. It disappears in 3 to 6 weeks even without treatment. Rash on the palms and soles is secondary.
questions.quote: Painless chancre (sore) at site of entry of germs, swollen glands

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the drug of choice for syphilis?
questions.rationale: Syphilis is treated with IM penicillin G benzathine; tetracycline or doxycycline are alternatives. The client completes treatment even after symptoms subside.
questions.quote: IM Penicillin G benzathine

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: A woman is prescribed metronidazole for trichomoniasis. What must the nurse teach?
questions.rationale: Alcohol is avoided while taking metronidazole and for 48 hours after, as the combination causes severe nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, and flushing.
questions.quote: avoid ingesting alcohol while taking metronidazole (and for 48 hours after completing the prescription)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which vaginal discharge is typical of trichomoniasis?
questions.rationale: Trichomoniasis causes a white or greenish-yellow odorous discharge with itching, soreness, and painful urination.
questions.quote: White or greenish – yellow odorous discharge

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A mother with untreated chlamydia delivers vaginally. Which newborn problem should the nurse watch for?
questions.rationale: Complications of chlamydia include infant eye infections and pneumonia, prematurity, and stillbirth. The newborn is assessed for chlamydial infection.
questions.quote: Eye Infections (infants)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why is gonorrhea often missed in women?
questions.rationale: About 80% of women with gonorrhea are asymptomatic, so case finding and partner treatment matter. Untreated infection can cause sterility and pelvic infection.
questions.quote: 80% are aysmptomatic

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: An infant has white curd-like patches on the tongue that bleed when scraped. What is this?
questions.rationale: Oral candidiasis (thrush) shows cream or bluish-white curd-like patches that reveal bloody engorgement when scraped. Milk curds wipe off easily.
questions.quote: curd-like patches of exudates on the tongue, mouth, or pharynx that reveal bloody engorgement when scraped

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: In the classic HIV testing sequence, which test is confirmatory?
questions.rationale: ELISA is the presumptive (screening) test and Western blot is the confirmatory test.
questions.quote: Western Blot – confirmatory test

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Which vector transmits dengue?
questions.rationale: Dengue is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Aedes aegypti mosquito.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 177)
questions.quote: Bite of female infected mosquito

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Which medicine should Kaye's mother AVOID for her fever?
questions.rationale: Aspirin is not given in dengue because it increases bleeding risk. An analgesic such as paracetamol and fluid replacement are used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 178)
questions.quote: Give analgesic (Don’t give Aspirin)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Kaye develops a nosebleed. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: For nosebleed in dengue, an ice bag is applied on the forehead and the bridge of the nose. The nurse also watches for shock.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 178)
questions.quote: Nose bleeding (apply ice bag on the forehead and at the bridge of the nose)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Which lab finding suggests plasma leakage in Kaye?
questions.rationale: Hemoconcentration, an increase of at least 20% in hematocrit, together with a falling platelet count, indicates plasma leakage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 177)
questions.quote: Hemoconcentration (increased of at least 20%)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which mosquito transmits malaria?
questions.rationale: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, and also by blood transfusion and across the placenta.
questions.quote: Transmitted mechanically through bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: A worker will go to a malaria-endemic area in Palawan. When should chloroquine prophylaxis start?
questions.rationale: Chloroquine is taken weekly, starting 1 to 2 weeks before entering the endemic area.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Malaria Chemoprophylaxis (PDF p. 179)
questions.quote: This must be taken at weekly intervals, starting from 1-2 weeks before entering endemic areas.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: Which teaching helps prevent malaria?
questions.rationale: Prevention includes insecticide-treated nets, house spraying, stream seeding and clearing, covering arms and legs in the evening, and avoiding outdoor night activity from 9 PM to 3 AM.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Malaria Prevention (PDF p. 179)
questions.quote: Avoiding outdoor night activities (9PM to 3AM)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: When is blood collected for the nocturnal blood examination (NBE) for filariasis?
questions.rationale: Microfilariae circulate at night, so NBE blood is taken at the client's residence from 8 PM. The ICT antigen test can be done in the daytime.
questions.quote: Blood are taken from the patient’s residence (8pm)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which drug is used to treat filariasis?
questions.rationale: Filariasis is treated with diethylcarbamazine citrate (Hetrazan), given as a yearly dose in mass treatment.
questions.quote: Diethylcarbamazine citrate (Hetrazan)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: After wading through floodwater with leg wounds, a man has fever, myalgia, and calf pain. What is suspected?
questions.rationale: Leptospirosis is a zoonosis spread when animal urine (mostly rats) contaminates water and enters through open skin. It is also called flood fever.
questions.quote: Direct contact on the skin through open wounds

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which drug is given as prophylaxis to people exposed to floodwater against leptospirosis?
questions.rationale: Doxycycline is used as prophylaxis for leptospirosis. Penicillin and tetracycline are used for treatment.
questions.quote: Doxycycline (Prophylactic)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the usual incubation period of rabies?
questions.rationale: Rabies usually incubates 3 to 8 weeks but ranges from 9 days to 7 years, depending on the virus dose, wound severity, and closeness to the brain.
questions.quote: 3 to 8 weeks, but may be as short as 9 days or as long as 7 years
